content.value_statement: TypeScript and Node.js projects need consistent standards for strict typing, performance, errors, and tests. This skill gives practical patterns for CLI tools, libraries, reviews, and refactors.
actual_capabilities: Defines strict TypeScript compiler settings for Node.js projects.
Shows safer typing with unknown, type guards, and explicit returns.
Explains async, streaming, and generator patterns for better performance.
Provides CLI structure guidance using Commander.js options and subcommands.
Recommends error handling with custom errors and Result types.
Includes Vitest testing patterns and review checklist items.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include executable helper scripts.
Examples need adaptation to each project architecture and dependency set.
It does not replace project-specific security review or threat modeling.
It focuses on TypeScript and Node.js, not browser frameworks or other runtimes.

use_cases.title: Create a CLI Tool
use_cases.description: Plan a typed Node.js CLI with Commander.js commands, options, errors, and tests.

use_cases.title: Review a TypeScript Module
use_cases.description: Check strict typing, async flow, error handling, test coverage, and maintainable module boundaries.

use_cases.title: Refactor for Performance
use_cases.description: Replace memory-heavy patterns with parallel async work, streams, and lazy collection processing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Strict Typing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one file or small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for strict typing, explicit return types, null safety, and simple fixes. Explain each issue before changing it.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CLI Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a new command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Node.js CLI command for this feature. Include command shape, option names, validation rules, error behavior, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Runtime Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor of a slow workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this module for performance. Look for sequential awaits, large in-memory reads, avoidable allocations, and streaming opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Library Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before release or major refactor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this library architecture. Evaluate module boundaries, dependency injection, exported types, error taxonomy, test strategy, and release readiness.

output_examples.input: Review a CLI command implementation for production readiness.
output: A ranked list of type safety, validation, and error handling issues.
A focused refactor plan that preserves the current command interface.
A test checklist covering happy paths, failures, and option parsing.

output_examples.input: Improve a module that reads large files and transforms records.
output: A performance assessment of memory use, async flow, and data copying.
A streaming-oriented plan with clear behavior and test expectations.
Notes about project-specific risks that still need human review.

output_examples.input: Plan a new TypeScript library package.
output: A concise package structure with public types and internal modules.
Guidance for errors, dependency injection, tests, and release checks.
A list of assumptions to confirm before implementation starts.

best_practices: Run the skill before TypeScript feature work, refactors, bug fixes, and reviews.
Share relevant tsconfig, package scripts, and test conventions with the agent.
Ask for focused changes when you need minimal churn in an existing codebase.
anti_patterns: Using broad prompts that ask for all improvements at once.
Accepting examples without adapting names, dependencies, and project conventions.
Skipping tests after changes that affect CLI behavior, IO, or error handling.

faq.question: Does this skill write code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent to produce and review TypeScript and Node.js code when asked.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with CLI projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Commander.js structure, option handling, user feedback, and validation patterns.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is guidance, and its fetch example is illustrative.

faq.question: Does it run npm commands?
faq.answer: It recommends verifying lint and tests, but command execution should follow the host agent permissions.

faq.question: Is it useful for library maintenance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers module organization, dependency injection, errors, performance, and test patterns.
